item.title: King’s Lynn runner completes ultra marathon for school garden project
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn runner completes ultra marathon for school garden project
A King’s Lynn man has raised £370 to help restore a sensory garden at Flitcham Primary Academy. John Costin completed the 35-mile Fields and Forests ultra marathon last Saturday, finishing the course through the Suffolk countryside and Thetford Forest in six hours and 38 minutes.
The funds will support the Friends of Flitcham Primary Academy in renovating the school’s garden, which has been in use for seven years. Mr. Costin launched the fundraiser to assist the school, which has 45 pupils, noting that small rural schools often face funding challenges. Donations for the project are still being accepted via his online fundraising page.

item.description:

Wisbech flats refurbished following council intervention
Seven flats in Wisbech have been renovated and are now occupied after Fenland District Council intervened to address poor living conditions. The properties, which previously suffered from significant damp and mould, were sold to a new landlord who completed the necessary refurbishments.
Council officials became involved after a tenant requested support, leading to the identification of the substandard housing. Fenland District Council is now encouraging residents living in poor conditions to come forward for assistance. The local authority investigates approximately 250 private rental properties annually and provides guidance to landlords regarding their legal obligations. Anyone concerned about their housing situation or aware of empty properties is urged to contact the council via their website.

item.title: Funding boost for historic King’s Lynn library restoration
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Funding boost for historic King’s Lynn library restoration
A major restoration project for the former Carnegie library in King’s Lynn has received a significant financial boost. The Workshop, which currently occupies the building, has secured a £249,000 grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund.
This funding will support the first phase of capital works, focusing on essential repairs to the roof, chimneys, windows, and the building’s historic parquet flooring. The project aims to preserve the site’s architectural character while improving energy efficiency. The Garage Trust, which operates the venue, intends to transform the landmark into a cultural hub for the community. Further investment has been provided by several other charitable trusts and individual donors to help secure the building's future as an arts centre.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/restoration-of-former-library-building-moves-forward-with-2-9483887/

Organised by the charity Classical Music Rocks, the event allowed children from Reception to Key Stage 2 to hear live music and learn about different instruments. The charity aims to introduce the genre to primary schools across Norfolk and Suffolk, having reached over 65,000 children since 2016.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court has dealt with a series of cases over the past week. Among those appearing was Carl Crawford, 38, of Walton Highway, who admitted to stealing over £5,000 from an elderly woman with Alzheimer’s disease. He will be sentenced at Norwich Crown Court at a later date.
Meanwhile, 51-year-old Mark Pleasants of Terrington St Clement is due for sentencing on November 5 after admitting to possessing indecent images of children and extreme images depicting rape.
